headline: Oklahoma State Park and Lake Entry Procedures
reservation: Beavers Bend State Park requires parking permits for all vehicles, which must be verified through the official state portal. Campsites and boat slips are managed via separate systems; verify all bookings with the Oklahoma Tourism and Recreation Department.

days.title: Wooded Bays and Open Water

stops.name: Stephens Gap Recreation Area
stops.detail: Access the lake's central basin for boating or enjoy the shoreline vistas from shaded picnic points.

stops.name: Carson Creek
stops.detail: Utilize the boat ramps or explore the quieter northern coves of the reservoir by kayak.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes; local roads near Hochatown experience significant weekend congestion.
days.note: Check lake levels and boat ramp status if water-based activities are your primary focus.

days.title: Lower Mountain Fork River Escapes

stops.name: Beavers Bend Dam Overlook
stops.detail: View the transition from the deep reservoir to the regulated trout waters of the Lower Mountain Fork.

stops.name: Forest Heritage Center
stops.detail: Tour indoor dioramas and historical exhibits focused on the forestry industry of the Kiamichi Mountains.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes; travel between the river and lake areas involves winding state park roads.
days.note: River flow is controlled by dam releases; check the official release schedule for safety.

days.title: Skyline Ridge and Shoreline Trails
days.start: Suggested: 8 AM from Beavers Bend State Park

stops.name: Skyline Trail
stops.detail: Hike the park's premier ridge route for views of the lake through the pine and oak canopy.

stops.name: Friends Trail
stops.detail: Take a moderate loop along the river bluffs for a close look at the regional geology.

days.driving: Walking within the park; allow 20 minutes for local transfers.
days.note: Ensure you carry sufficient water as trails can be humid and strenuous during summer months.

intel.title: State Park Parking Permits
intel.text: Beavers Bend State Park utilizes a digital parking payment system. Ensure your license plate is registered at official kiosks or via the mobile site to avoid citations.

intel.title: Connectivity Limits
intel.text: Cell service is strong in Hochatown but fades significantly near the lake’s northern reaches. Map your route to remote boat ramps before leaving the main highway.

intel.title: Hochatown Supply Logic
intel.text: Gas and provisions are best secured in Hochatown or the town of Broken Bow. Few services exist once you enter the state park or deep forest roads.

intel.title: Holiday Congestion
intel.text: Expect significant delays on Highway 259 during Memorial Day and Labor Day weekends. Early morning starts are suggested to secure boat ramp access.

intel.title: River Safety
intel.text: Wading in the Mountain Fork River requires awareness of dam sirens. Immediate evacuation of the riverbed is required when sirens indicate a water release.

plan.arrival: Arrive at Texarkana Regional Airport (TXK) and drive approximately 2 hours to Hochatown for cabin check-in and supplies.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are suitable for the paved park roads, but check cabin access descriptions as some gravel driveways require higher clearance.
plan.goldenHour: Sunset from the Mountain Fork bridge offers a scenic perspective, though colors are highly dependent on seasonal humidity.
